bifurcation.note: Protocol A is the FIDELITY side and refuses Morrowind imagery. No art-direction reference was consulted, no Morrowind image was opened, and Protocol B has still never been run by any agent in this project — RI-VIS06's side declaration voids both results if one agent runs both. score.band_label: Below bar — the wave is blocked again, and the diagnosis is now the remedy

biggest_gap.what: Protocol A re-ran five pairs after F1 (PBR materials), F2 (contact shadows + AO) and F3 (ambient/GI fill) all landed and each measured green on its own instrument — per orchestration/status/I3-PROTOCOL-A-R2-RESULT.json: orphaned surface materials 321/422 to 0; contact-junction ratio 0.722 against a >=25% bar; ambient lift +0.631 replicated across three GPUs with the control at -0.001. The blind result did not move: 0 of 5 again, four judges at CONFIDENCE high and one at medium (unchanged spread from r1), and the aggregate synthesis of all five judges again names the same two absences r1 found — no material differentiation between surfaces ('every surface returns the same flat matte olive-grey', 'thatch, plaster, stone and ground all return light identically', 'nothing reads as leather, metal, stone or vegetation') and no contact darkening or cast shadow ('no contact darkening and no cast shadows at all, so nothing sits in space', 'surfaces meet with no contact darkening'). The mechanical local_contrast_med statistic still sweeps 5/5 toward the reference on the same channel r1's leak-check also swept 5/5.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The remedies exist in the codebase and pass their own numeric gates, but a player looking at the world still sees what the r1 judges saw: every surface responding to light the same way, and nothing casting a contact shadow. An instrument passing its own gate has stopped being evidence that the player-visible problem is fixed, which is exactly the failure RI-VIS06 exists to catch.

remedy.action: Diagnose why F1/F2/F3 do not visibly change the five captured setups Protocol A draws from, BEFORE building anything new — per I3-PROTOCOL-A-R2-RESULT.json's own next_step. Re-render the exact five capture setups (char-npc and char-player at 08:00/13:00/19:30) with AO forced to full strength — uAOMaxOcclusion set to 1.0 instead of its current 0.6 cap (uAOStrength 3.1, radius 0.42) — and with all 20 authored material sets forced bound, and diff the result against the shipped configuration. If the terrain-artifact cap named in I3-PROTOCOL-A-R2-RESULT.json is confirmed as the cause (the cap was added deliberately to hide a derivative-normal grid artifact on low-poly terrain, and several of these pairs are terrain/vegetation-heavy), the remedy moves to the G-buffer normal-target limitation F2's own verdict already named as unsolved.
remedy.acceptance: A forced-full-strength render (uAOMaxOcclusion=1.0, all 20 material sets bound) of the same five capture setups shows a measurable difference from the shipped configuration on image-leakcheck's own quality statistics (local_contrast_med and shadow_levels move outside their current per-pair values by more than the tool's tie margin); AND the next Protocol A re-run's five judges' aggregate synthesis no longer names both 'no material differentiation' and 'no contact shadow / AO' as recurring absences.

secondary_observations.what: The positional-bias check is now genuinely full-power, not merely deterministic-bias-ruled-out. r1's free coin flip left one discriminating trial; r2's counterbalanced design (ours on A for pairs 01/03/05, B for 02/04, fixed before any image was opened) means any constant-letter strategy could match the reference on at most 3 of 5 pairs, and the observed match was 5 of 5. This is the payoff of r1's reversible ruling and should be kept for round 3.

Two leaks were caught before any judge saw the pack, and neither was caught by the automated gate. F1: a HUD region name-plate ('western-rootlands') had begun drawing into two of five crop windows since r1's capture; image-leakcheck was GREEN on the version containing legible burnt-in text, because a handful of text pixels move no summary statistic. F3, run deliberately to test the gate: a quantised leak on every pair goes RED, but the identical injection on only ONE pair goes GREEN and is missed — the battery is a sweep detector, and a leak affecting fewer than all pairs is invisible to it however blatant it is. RI-VIS06 §D's HUD row is currently enforced by eye and by nothing else.

Our r2 crops are 25-30% larger than the same windows in r1 (pair01 330,353 -> 422,286 bytes; pair03 340,860 -> 442,253 bytes), because real material detail and an occlusion term cost bytes while the JPEG-sourced reference crops are byte-identical to r1's. The bytes channel swept RED 5/5 on the first r2 pack build before an active zero-filled-chunk equalisation brought it to a tie. r1's own pack was one pair short of the same sweep (4 of 5), which in hindsight means r1's leak-check result was closer to a void condition than its verdict recorded.

gap_closure.measured_value: Still named by the aggregate of all five r2 judges as an absence — 'every surface returns the same flat matte olive-grey', 'thatch, plaster, stone and ground all return light identically', 'nothing reads as leather, metal, stone or vegetation' — after F1 (the remedy this gap named) landed and measured green on its own instrument (orphaned surface materials 321/422 to 0, per I3-PROTOCOL-A-R2-RESULT.json, not independently re-derived here).
gap_closure.acceptance_restated: Two named materials in a single capture from the fixed eight slots produce measurably different specular response under the same light; and a Protocol A re-run returns 'everything responds to light identically' as no pair's SINGLE BIGGEST GAP.
gap_closure.note: Re-measured by this verdict, which built nothing and judged nothing, so the closure attempt is valid under SCORING.md §5 rule 1 regardless of outcome. Recorded as still OPEN, not closed and not partially-closed: the acceptance clause's own text was not met. This re-measurement happened one wave early — the acceptance text names a wave-2 re-run and this is a second run still within wave 1 — which this verdict states plainly rather than treating the early result as if it satisfied a wave-2 condition. A further limitation: this verdict does not have r2's per-pair breakdown of which absence was named as SINGLE BIGGEST versus SECOND GAP (no JUDGEMENTS-r2.md file exists), so it cannot say with the same precision as r1 whether material differentiation was any pair's single biggest gap this round — only that it was named in the aggregate synthesis. Superseded in practical terms by GAP-W1-visual-fix-not-reaching-blind-frames, which is the sharper, more buildable statement of the same underlying problem now that its own remedy has landed without effect — but this entry is left OPEN rather than marked 'superseded', because GAP-W1-visual-fix-not-reaching-blind-frames is a diagnosis-first gap about why the fix doesn't reach these frames, not a strictly harder version of the original material-binding gap, and superseding requires the latter.

Ours lost again, so a losing verdict is strengthened by this deviation, not weakened. Owed remedy unchanged: run the judges from a working directory with no project CLAUDE.md in scope.

method_deviations.deviation: D3/D4 (carried from r1, deliberately not fixed) — pair02/pair03's reference windows are still out-of-focus background bokeh, and pair05's subject scale still mismatches (near-field material close-up vs our mid-distance dusk walkway, drawn from the weakest source frame in the pack).
method_deviations.why: The pack-builder deliberately did NOT apply r1's owed D3/D4 remedies (swapping either plate), per I3-PROTOCOL-A-RERUN.json's N4: a changed pair could not be read against r1's answer on the same pair, which is the entire point of running r2 as a comparison. Cost stated plainly: r2 inherits both confounds. Owed remedy unchanged from r1: an in-focus daylight exterior plate for pair02/pair03, a low-light mid-distance exterior plate for pair05.

method_deviations.deviation: D6 — an ACTIVE byte-length equalisation was applied to every pair, and this is not evidence of blindness.
method_deviations.why: image-leakcheck's bytes channel swept RED 5/5 on the first r2 pack build: our PNGs run 25-30% larger than r1's at the same crop windows, because real material detail and an occlusion term carry more high-frequency content than a JPEG-sourced reference crop whose DCT quantisation has already smoothed it. protocol-a-pack.mjs --equalise-bytes padded each arm with a zero-filled private ancillary PNG chunk until both files in a pair were byte-identical in length; pixels are untouched and every quality statistic is unchanged by the padding. Because this equalisation is ACTIVE rather than incidental, the resulting bytes tie (0/0, 5 tied) in leakcheck-r2.txt is true by construction and must not be read as evidence the pack was naturally unsortable by file size — it was sortable, and the improvement under test is exactly what tripped the gate. Separately worth recording: r1's own pack escaped this same sweep by one pair (4 of 5, not 5 of 5), which in hindsight means r1's leak-check GREEN was one pair away from the same RED this pack hit before equalisation, and r1's verdict did not know this at the time.

method_deviations.deviation: D7 — a HUD region name-plate leak was found by opening the crops, not by the leak-check tool, and fixed before any judge saw the pack; the tool's own limit (a sweep detector) was then confirmed by deliberate injection.
method_deviations.why: The build now draws a region name ('western-rootlands') into the canvas at x 42-180, y 962-983 — new since r1's capture on 2026-08-14 — and r1's crop window at (150,480), reused for r2's pair02 and pair04, caught its last two glyphs. Two of five arms would have shipped with legible burnt-in text. image-leakcheck was GREEN on the contaminated version, because a few dozen text pixels move no summary statistic. The fix (window moved to (200,480), a 50px translation) was applied BEFORE the pack was built and BEFORE any judge ran, so it does not affect this run's scores directly — recorded here because it changes what the judged pack looked like relative to any earlier, undocumented window, and because the pack-builder went on to prove by deliberate injection (three leaky copies of the real pack, isolating one channel each) that the same gate misses a leak present on only one of five pairs while catching the identical leak swept across all five. That is a standing limit of the instrument, not a defect specific to this pack.

self_audit.self_audit_note: This verdict built nothing and judged nothing, mirroring r1's chunk-2 role: the five judges answered before this verdict began, and this verdict's job was to read the already-decoded result correctly, not to re-judge it. conflict_of_interest is false because none of the work under judgement — the renderer, F1/F2/F3, the pack, the frames — was written or edited by this agent. Two things are disclosed here because the task explicitly required them and because smoothing them into the score would be dishonest: (1) the judges could not be made naive — a subagent in this repository inherits the project CLAUDE.md — and the pack-builder reasoned that this bias flatters our side, so a LOSS is strengthened by it, not weakened; ours lost. (2) three of the five judges (per the aggregate synthesis in I3-PROTOCOL-A-R2-RESULT.json) volunteered that our arm holds sharper silhouette edges and better fine detail while the reference plates are heavily blurred JPEGs — so this loss is demonstrably not about resolution, aliasing or sharpness, all of which our side wins; it is specifically about material response and light. 'escalation_ladder_used_if_gap_seemed_small' is true vacuously and deliberately, as in r1: RI-VIS06 §C's escalation fires only if ours wins a pair, and ours won none.
